The <hi type="italic">conviction</hi> which Christ gave his apostles of the truth of his resurrection (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.14">v. 14</reference>); He <hi type="italic">appeared to them</hi> himself, when they were all together, <hi type="italic">as they sat at meat,</hi> which gave him an opportunity to <hi type="italic">eat and drink with them,</hi> for their full satisfaction; see <reference osisRef="Acts.10.41">Acts x. 41</reference>. And still, when he appeared to them, he <hi type="italic">upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart,</hi> for even at the general meeting in <hi type="italic">Galilee, some doubted,</hi> as we find <reference osisRef="Matt.28.17">Matt. xxviii. 17</reference>. Note, The evidences of the truth of the gospel are so full, that those who receive it not, may justly be <hi type="italic">upbraided</hi> with their unbelief; and it is owing not to any weakness or deficiency in the proofs, but to the <hi type="italic">hardness of their heart,</hi> its senselessness and stupidity. Though they had not till now seen him themselves, they are justly blamed <hi type="italic">because they believed not them who had seen him after he was risen;</hi> and perhaps it was owing in part to the <hi type="italic">pride of their hearts,</hi> that they did not; for they thought, "If indeed he be risen, to <hi type="italic">whom should he delight to do</hi> the <hi type="italic">honour</hi> of showing himself but to us?" And if he <hi type="italic">pass them by,</hi> and show himself to <hi type="italic">others</hi> first, they cannot believe it is he. Thus many disbelieve the doctrine of Christ, because they think it <hi type="italic">below them</hi> to give credit to such as he had chosen to be the witnesses and publishers of it. Observe, It will not suffice for an excuse of our infidelity in the great day, to say, "<hi type="italic">We did not see him</hi> after he was risen," for we ought to have believed the testimony of those who did see him. <div eID="gen25074" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25075" type="x-p"/> II. The <hi type="italic">commission</hi> which he gave them to set up his kingdom among men by the preaching of his <hi type="italic">gospel,</hi> the glad tidings of reconciliation to God through a Mediator. Now observe, <div eID="gen25075" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25076" type="x-p"/> 1. <hi type="italic">To whom</hi> they were to preach <hi type="italic">the gospel.</hi> Hitherto they had been sent only to <hi type="italic">the lost sheep of the house of Israel,</hi> and were forbidden to go into the <hi type="italic">way of the Gentiles,</hi> or into any city of the Samaritans; but now their commission is enlarged, and they are authorized to <hi type="italic">go into all the world,</hi> into all parts of the world, the habitable world, and to <hi type="italic">preach the gospel</hi> of Christ to <hi type="italic">every creature,</hi> to the Gentiles as well as to the Jews; to every human creature that is capable of receiving it. "Inform them concerning Christ, the history of <hi type="italic">his life,</hi> and <hi type="italic">death,</hi> and <hi type="italic">resurrection;</hi> instruct them in the <hi type="italic">meaning</hi> and <hi type="italic">intention</hi> of these, and of the advantages which the children of men have, or may have, hereby; and invite them, without exception, to come and share in them. This is <hi type="italic">gospel.</hi> Let this be <hi type="italic">preached</hi> in all places, to all persons." These eleven men could not themselves preach it to all the world, much less to <hi type="italic">every creature</hi> in it; but they and the other disciples, seventy in number, with those who should afterward to be added to them, must <hi type="italic">disperse</hi> themselves several ways, and, wherever they went, carry the gospel along with them. They must send <hi type="italic">others</hi> to those places whither they could not <hi type="italic">go themselves,</hi> and, in short, make it the business of their lives to send those glad tidings <hi type="italic">up and down the world</hi> with all possible fidelity and care, not as an amusement or entertainment, but as a solemn message from God to men, and an appointed means of making men happy. "Tell as many as you can, and bid them tell others; it is a message of universal concern, and <hi type="italic">therefore,</hi> ought to <hi type="italic">have</hi> a universal welcome, because it <hi type="italic">gives</hi> a universal welcome." <div eID="gen25076" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25077" type="x-p"/> 2. What is the <hi type="italic">summary of the gospel</hi> they are to preach (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.16">v. 16</reference>); "Set before the world life and death, good and evil. Tell the children of men that they are all in a state of misery and danger, <hi type="italic">condemned</hi> by their prince, and <hi type="italic">conquered</hi> and <hi type="italic">enslaved</hi> by their enemies." This is supposed in their being <hi type="italic">saved,</hi> which they would not need to be if they were not <hi type="italic">lost.</hi> "Now go and tell them," (1.) "That if they <hi type="italic">believe the gospel,</hi> and give up themselves to be Christ's disciples; if they <hi type="italic">renounce</hi> the devil, the world, and the flesh, and be <hi type="italic">devoted</hi> to Christ as their prophet, priest, and king, and to God in Christ a their God in covenant, and evidence by their constant adherence to this covenant their sincerity herein, they <hi type="italic">shall be saved</hi> from the guilt and power of sin, it shall not <hi type="italic">rule</hi> them, it shall not <hi type="italic">ruin</hi> them. He that is a true Christian, shall be saved through Christ." <hi type="italic">Baptism</hi> was appointed to be the <hi type="italic">inaugurating</hi> rite, by which those that embraced Christ owned him; but it is here put rather for the <hi type="italic">thing signified</hi> than for the sign, for Simon Magus <hi type="italic">believed</hi> and was <hi type="italic">baptized,</hi> yet was not <hi type="italic">saved,</hi> <reference osisRef="Acts.8.13">Acts viii. 13</reference>. <hi type="italic">Believing with the heart, and confessing with the mouth the Lord Jesus</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rom.10.9">Rom. x. 9</reference>), seems to be much the same with this here. Or thus, We must <hi type="italic">as</hi>sent to gospel-truths, and <hi type="italic">con</hi>sent to gospel-terms. (2.) "<hi type="italic">If they believe not,</hi> if they receive not the record God gives concerning his Son, they cannot expect any other way of salvation, but must inevitably perish; <hi type="italic">they shall be damned,</hi> by the sentence of a <hi type="italic">despised</hi> gospel, added to that of a broken law." And even this is <hi type="italic">gospel,</hi> it is good news, that nothing else but unbelief shall damn men, which is a sin against the remedy. Dr. Whitby here observes, that they who hence infer "that the infant seed of believers are not capable of baptism, because they cannot believe, must hence also infer that they cannot be saved; <hi type="italic">faith</hi> being here more expressly required to salvation than to baptism. And that in the latter clause baptism is omitted, because it is not simply the want of baptism, but the contemptuous neglect of it, which makes men guilty of damnation, otherwise infants might be damned for the mistakes or profaneness of their parents." <div eID="gen25077" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25078" type="x-p"/> 3. What power they should be endowed with, for the confirmation of the doctrine they were to preach (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.17">v. 17</reference>); <hi type="italic">These signs shall follow them that believe.</hi> Not that all who believe, shall be able to produce these signs, but some, even as many as were employed in propagating the faith, and bringing others to it; for signs are intended <hi type="italic">for them that believe not;</hi> see <reference osisRef="1Cor.14.22">1 Cor. xiv. 22</reference>. It added much to the glory and evidence of the gospel, that the preachers not only wrought miracles themselves, but conferred upon others a power to work miracles, which power <hi type="italic">followed</hi> some of them that believed, wherever they went to preach. They shall do wonders <hi type="italic">in Christ's name,</hi> the same name into which they were baptized, in the virtue of power derived from him, and fetched in by prayer. Some particular signs are mentioned; (1.) They shall <hi type="italic">cast out devils;</hi> this power was more common among Christians than any other, and lasted longer, as appears by the testimonies of Justin Martyr, Origen, Irenæus, Tertullian Minutius Felix, and others, cited by Grotius on this place. (2.) They shall <hi type="italic">speak with new tongues,</hi> which they had never learned, or been acquainted with; and this was both a <hi type="italic">miracle</hi> (a miracle <hi type="italic">upon the mind</hi>), for the confirming of the truth of the gospel, and a <hi type="italic">means</hi> of spreading the gospel among those nations that had not heard it. It saved the preachers a vast labour in learning the languages; and, no doubt, they who by <hi type="italic">miracle</hi> were made <hi type="italic">masters of languages,</hi> were <hi type="italic">complete</hi> masters of them and of all their native elegancies, which were proper both to <hi type="italic">instruct</hi> and <hi type="italic">affect,</hi> which would very much recommend them and their preaching. (3.) They shall <hi type="italic">take up serpents.</hi> This was fulfilled in Paul, who was not hurt by the <hi type="italic">viper</hi> that <hi type="italic">fastened on his hand,</hi> which was acknowledged a great miracle by the barbarous people, <reference osisRef="Acts.28.5-Acts.28.6">Acts xxviii. 5, 6</reference>. They shall be kept unhurt by that <hi type="italic">generation of vipers</hi> among whom they live, and by the malice of the <hi type="italic">old serpent.</hi> (4.) If they be compelled by their persecutors to <hi type="italic">drink any deadly</hi> poisonous thing, <hi type="italic">it shall not hurt them:</hi> of which very thing some instances are found in ecclesiastical history. (5.) They shall not only be preserved from hurt themselves, but they shall be enabled to do good to others; <hi type="italic">They shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover,</hi> as multitudes had done by their master's <hi type="italic">healing</hi> touch. Many of the elders of the church had this power, as appears by <reference osisRef="Jas.5.14">Jam. v. 14</reference>, where, as an instituted sign of this miraculous healing, they are said to <hi type="italic">anoint</hi> the sick <hi type="italic">with oil in the name of the Lord.</hi> With what assurance of success might they go about executing their commission, when they had such credentials as these to produce!

<div eID="gen25078" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Ascension.</title> <div sID="gen25079" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">19</hi> So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God. 20 And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with <hi type="italic">them,</hi> and confirming the word with signs following. Amen. <div eID="gen25079" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25080" type="x-p"/> Here is, 1. Christ <hi type="italic">welcomed</hi> into the <hi type="italic">upper world</hi> (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.19">v. 19</reference>): <hi type="italic">After the Lord had spoken</hi> what he had to say to his disciples, he <hi type="italic">went up into heaven,</hi> in a cloud; which we have a particular account of (<reference osisRef="Acts.1.9">Acts i. 9</reference>), and he had not only an admission, but an abundant <hi type="italic">entrance,</hi> into his kingdom there; he was <hi type="italic">received up,</hi> received in state, with loud acclamations of the heavenly hosts; and he <hi type="italic">sat on the right hand of God:</hi> sitting in a posture of <hi type="italic">rest,</hi> for now he had finished his work, and a posture of <hi type="italic">rule,</hi> for now he took possession of his kingdom; he sat <hi type="italic">at the right hand of God,</hi> which denotes the sovereign dignity he is advanced to, and the universal agency he is entrusted with. Whatever God does concerning us, gives to us, or accepts from us, it is <hi type="italic">by his Son.</hi> Now he is glorified with the glory he had before the world. <div eID="gen25080" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25081" type="x-p"/> 2. Christ <hi type="italic">welcomed</hi> in this <hi type="italic">lower world;</hi> his being <hi type="italic">believed on in the world,</hi> and <hi type="italic">received up into glory,</hi> are put together, <reference osisRef="1Tim.3.16">1 Tim. iii. 16</reference>. (1.) We have here the apostles working diligently for him; they <hi type="italic">went forth, and preached every where</hi> far and near. Though the doctrine they preached, was <hi type="italic">spiritual</hi> and <hi type="italic">heavenly,</hi> and directly contrary to the <hi type="italic">spirit</hi> and <hi type="italic">genius</hi> of the world, though it met with abundance of opposition, and was utterly destitute of all secular supports and advantages, yet the preachers of it were neither <hi type="italic">afraid</hi> nor <hi type="italic">ashamed;</hi> they were so industrious in spreading the gospel, that within a few years the sound of it <hi type="italic">went forth into the ends of the earth,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rom.10.18">Rom. x. 18</reference>. (2.) We have here God <hi type="italic">working</hi> effectually <hi type="italic">with them,</hi> to make their labours successful, by <hi type="italic">confirming the word with signs following,</hi> partly by the miracles that were wrought upon the <hi type="italic">bodies</hi> of the people, which were divine seals to the Christian doctrine, and partly by the influence it had upon the <hi type="italic">minds</hi> of the people, through the operation of the Spirit of God, see <reference osisRef="Heb.2.4">Heb. ii. 4</reference>. These were properly <hi type="italic">signs following</hi> the word—the reformation of the world, the destruction of idolatry, the conversion of sinners, the comfort of saints; and these signs still follow it, and that they may do so more and more, for the honour of Christ and the good of mankind, the evangelist prays, and teaches us to say <hi type="italic">Amen.</hi> Father in heaven, thus let thy name be hallowed, and let thy kingdom come.  <chapter eID="Mark.16"/> <div eID="gen25081" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen24289" osisID="Mark" type="book"/>
